messages:
Dmitri: Quick heads-up — tried an nsys capture inside a rootless k8s pod to profile kernel selection + KV cache hotspot for the new batching heuristics, but the capture came back with no kernel samples and missing NVTX markers. Using nvidia-container-toolkit 2.11, runtimeClass node-runtime-rootless, pod has no privileged=true. Anyone hit this before?

Carla: This is pretty common if the process can't attach to the driver or the toolkit mount points are root-only. Two quick options: run the capture in a privileged pod, or use an initContainer to fix perms on the capture dir so nvprof/nsys can write. Also try --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi if NVTX is missing. Example initContainer snippet we use: 

```yaml
initContainers:
  - name: chown-nvprof
    image: busybox
    command: ["sh", "-c", "chown -R 1000:1000 /tmp/nvprof || true"]
    volumeMounts:
      - name: nvprof-tmp
        mountPath: /tmp/nvprof
```

That avoids privileged in many cases. :thumbsup:

Ben: For the long-running batching workload we also switched to perfetto for lower overhead sampling (nsys has higher perturbation). perfetto can collect cgroup events and kernel ftrace samples which helped us find kernel-level memcpy hotspots that weren't obvious in nsys. Example perfetto cli: 

```bash
perfetto record -o /tmp/trace.pftrace --txt -c "-e cpu:cpu_clock -f 2000" 
# then: trace_processor_shell /tmp/trace.pftrace
```

The trace_processor sql lets you aggregate by stack and find the heavy matmul/cuBLAS kernels.

Emma: Note: after the kernel-selection change we saw nsys not attributing some kernels to cuBLAS because the runtime dynamically switched to cuBLASLt kernels (different symbol names). In nsys use --sample=kernel and add a filter for cuBLAS/cuBLASLt symbols, or run with --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi and insert NVTX around the op in the runtime so the profiler knows where to correlate. Example nsys command we run: 

```bash
nsys profile --output /tmp/nsys.qdrep --sample=kernel --sample-freq=1000
  --trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt --target-processes all --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi
  -- ./bin/runtime --profile-target mymodel
```

Emma: Also double-check the nvidia-container-toolkit mounts: /run/nvidia and /var/lib/nvidia are often root-owned. If you want to keep rootless, try setting securityContext.fsGroup on the pod or add mountOptions in the DaemonSet so the runtime uid can access them. Example: 

```yaml
securityContext:
  runAsUser: 1000
  fsGroup: 1000
```

Dmitri: Good tips — I'll try the initContainer chown + capture-range first. If that fails I'll spin a privileged debug pod to rule out toolkit mount issues. One last question: is CAP_SYS_PTRACE sufficient or do we need full privileged? :thinking:

Carla: CAP_SYS_PTRACE + CAP_SYS_ADMIN sometimes, but it depends on the node/runtime config and selinux/apparmor. Privileged is blunt but works. CAP_SYS_PTRACE is safer if you want to minimize blast radius.

infra-bot: Debug job started: debug/pod-profiling-1769123456 — kubelet scheduled on node-gpu-3 (pod/ debug logs forwarded to /var/log/profiling).

Dmitri: Thanks all — I'll post the nsys and perfetto traces here once I get reproducible samples. :raised_hands:
